# Path Crossing.

@example Her corners are (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1), (2, 0), (1, 0), and then (1, 1) again.
"NEESWN"
=> true

@example The start and the corners (1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1), (1, 1), (0, 1) and (-1, 1) are all different.
"EENWWW"
=> false

@example Four steps around one block bring her back to (0, 0), where she started.
"SWNE"
=> true

# A single step never repeats a corner.
"W"
=> false

# Two steps repeat a corner only when the second goes straight back.
"NS"
=> true

"EW"
=> true

"SE"
=> false

# The only repeat is the start, reached by the last step of a big loop.
"NNNEEESSSWWW"
=> true

# An inward spiral passes next to earlier corners without landing on one.
"EENNWWSE"
=> false

# One step more, and she lands on (1, 0), reached by her first step.
"EENNWWSES"
=> true

# All four letters. Taking N and E as the same direction would repeat (0, 3).
"NNEESW"
=> false

# A staircase of 1000 steps that never repeats, then one step straight back.
""
=> true

# One step east, then a loop of 5000 blocks round a square that closes on
# (1, 0), her first corner, with its very last step. Every other corner is
# new, so a check of only the latest corners, or a set that stops taking
# corners when it fills up, misses it.
""
=> true

# 260 steps west: a coordinate kept in 8 bits would wrap round to 0.
"WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW"
=> false

# The longest route, all east: x reaches 10^4.
""
=> false

# One step east, then 9999 south. (1, -9999) is a new corner, although
# a key x * 9999 + y would give it the same value as (0, 0).
""
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"NSSNWWWWN"
=> true

@gen 2 small
"NWWNNNS"
=> true

@gen 3 small
"NWSWWN"
=> false

@gen 4 small
"SENE"
=> false

@gen 5 small
"SENESENNNW"
=> false

@gen 6 small
"ES"
=> false
